captions.intro_sub: The game's own nation builder, as in 1987
captions.outro_sub: Ask for an invite · found your nation tonight

segments.text: Before your first turn, you found your nation. The first time you play, the game opens its own nation builder, the same one players met in nineteen eighty-seven. It takes two minutes. Here is how.
First, the name of your nation, up to nine letters. Every ruler will see it on the map. Type it and press Enter.
Now a password for your nation, up to seven characters. Nothing shows while you type. The game asks for it every time you play, so keep it.
The name of your ruler. The news will speak of them.
Choose a race with one letter: dwarves, elves, humans or orcs. Humans are balanced, the easiest to begin with.
Your class. Type its number and press Enter. King and emperor cost no points, and suit a first game.
Good, neutral or evil. It shapes how the nations of the computer see you.
One letter marks your land on everyone's map.
Now, the points. Each line is something your nation can buy. J moves down, K moves up, and Space buys one more of the marked line.
A tip: buy two points of treasury. A nation without gold cannot draft troops in its first turn. Press Escape when you are done.
segments.title: Buy some gold

segments.text: The points you did not spend can become people. Press Y, then any key.
Is your nation as you want it? Press Y.
Save it with Y. Careful: any other key deletes the nation, and you start again.
Your nation is in the world. From now on, Play takes you straight to it, and the game asks for its password.
That is all. Ask for an invite code, create your account, and found your nation. Then, your first turn.
